newsitem.title: UK: Security forces find bomb parts - N.Irish police.
newsitem.headline: Security forces find bomb parts - N.Irish police.

text.p: Police in Northern Ireland said they found guerrilla bomb-making equipment in a lorry abandoned near the border with the Irish Republic on Monday.

A police spokesman said a small quantity of explosives and "booster tubes", which guerrillas battling British rule in the province use to set off powerful home-made bombs, had been found on the vehicle near Roslea village in County Fermanagh.
It was the latest in a series of arms finds which have fuelled fears of a new bombing campaign by the Irish Republican Army (IRA) or other outlawed Irish nationalist groups.
Police and soldiers spent a week checking out the lorry and a nearby vehicle both of which had been stolen elsewhere in the province.

Last week police accused republican fighters of trying to lure security forces into a foiled mortar ambush in north Belfast. A trailer load of explosives was found near a military barracks in County Armagh.

IRA guerrillas killed a soldier in a double bomb blast inside Britain's military garrison at Lisburn south of Belfast in October. Security has been tightened province-wide and in mainland Britain in case of further attacks.

A breakaway group, the Irish Continuity Army Council tried to blow up police headquarters in the region's second city, Londonderry in November, but British bomb disposal officers managed to defuse the guerrillas' car bomb.

The hostilies have dealt a bitter blow to struggling political efforts to secure a new IRA ceasefire and resurrect a three-year-old peace process. The IRA bombed targets on mainland Britain last February, ending a 17-month truce.
The province's 60 per cent Protestant population support rule from London but the minority Roman Catholics want an all-Ireland state ruled from Dublin.
